subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should automatic stalled-subagent recovery be added now as default-on runtime behavior, and should it live in the subagent registry/diagnostics path or wait for the sessions.activity/watchdog design?
rationale: The remaining work changes default kill behavior, adds or repurposes config surface, and decides user-visible recovery semantics across subagents, sessions, diagnostics, and chat channels; that is a product/compatibility choice, not a narrow repair.

options.title: Approve a runtime recovery contract
options.body: Implement deterministic subagent stall recovery with conservative defaults, visible parent/channel terminal delivery, and docs/tests that prove upgrade and normal long-run behavior.

options.title: Fold into sessions.activity/watchdog
options.body: Keep this issue open as a requirement on the activity/watchdog track so alerts, recovery, and channel UX share one owner model.

options.title: Keep diagnostics-only mitigation
options.body: Do not add subagent-specific nudge/kill behavior and rely on existing generic diagnostic aborts plus manual kill paths, accepting the remaining UX gap.

recommendation.title: Approve a runtime recovery contract
recommendation.body: Implement deterministic subagent stall recovery with conservative defaults, visible parent/channel terminal delivery, and docs/tests that prove upgrade and normal long-run behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent cross-boundary subagent, session-kill, and runtime history and is the best available owner for the product/config direction call.
